source_refs.note: Topic printed as 7.10, printed pages 197-198: tropic movements and the four tropisms.

blocks.text: Organisms react to external and internal stimuli. Animals may move from place to place in response, but plants are fixed, so they can only alter their pattern of growth.

blocks.title: Tropic movements
blocks.text: The growth movements of plants triggered by a stimulus are collectively called tropic movements or tropisms. They occur as a curvature of the whole organ towards or away from a stimulus such as light, touch, chemicals, water and gravity.

items: Phototropism is the movement of a plant part in response to light, caused by the differential growth of a part such as a stem or root. Shoot tips usually show positive phototropism, roots negative phototropism.
Geotropism is movement in response to gravity: roots show positive geotropism and shoots negative geotropism.

Thigmotropism is movement in response to touch, as in climbing vines: when a tendril touches a solid object, growth on the side away from the contact increases and the tendril coils round the support.
Chemotropism is movement in response to chemicals; the hyphae of fungi are chemotropic.
